handoff_record.next_agent_notes: Step 2 is a free gateway model driving these operations behind the crisis gate, streamed to the chat page, behind whatever access control the owner picks. Create the sandbox through withAgentSandbox/agentSandboxParams(): the defaults allow only the package-registry and GitHub presets (pass egressPresets: [] for deny-all), the name is fixed, and the work function receives an AbortSignal it must honor. Never pass host env or credentials into the sandbox. Keep the policy review inside the operations; do not add a path around it. Do not use @vercel/sandbox 3.7.0+ until the zod advisory chain is fixed. Timeout expiry behavior of sandbox.runCommand (rejects vs exit code 137) was not verified against a live sandbox. Step 2: Pi createAgentSession accepts customTools, noTools:'builtin', model, modelRuntime, sessionManager and settingsManager, so the sandbox operations can be passed via createBashToolDefinition etc. with in-memory session and settings. The gateway accepts the Vercel OIDC token as a Bearer token on /v1/chat/completions; read it with getVercelOidcToken() from @vercel/oidc inside the request (not at module level), pin it to 3.2.0 (the version @vercel/sandbox 3.6.1 uses; 3.6.0 to 4.0.5 is in an audited range). Pi's bundled vercel-ai-gateway model list is a snapshot and does not track free models, so build the model entry from the live catalog. Previews are behind Vercel login again, so curl against a preview returns 302; the route cannot be tested live from the agent session without the owner's help. Pi's createAgentSession takes modelRuntime/model/customTools/sessionManager/settingsManager; ModelRuntime is file-backed (auth.json, models.json), and pi-ai exports a faux provider (registerFauxProvider, fauxAssistantMessage, fauxToolCall) that Pi's own session tests use, which allows testing the runner offline. Update: the whole project is behind Vercel login (all deployments), including production, so the agent route is gated by an owner-set per-environment flag (off by default). Previews and production both return 302/401 to automated callers, so live tests of the route need the owner.
